newsitem.title: japan: Matsushita's profits surge, helped by weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita's profits surge, helped by weak yen.

text.p: Consumer electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. said Tuesday that strong demand for high-tech products and a weak yen helped its profits surge in its fiscal third quarter.

Matsushita -- whose products are sold under the National, Panasonic and Technics brand names -- also announced a sweeping measure to rid itself of bad loans made to its troubled finance unit, NL Finance, during Japan's economic "bubble" of the 1980s that burt in the early 1990s.

The company said it would write off long-term loans to NL Finance worth 100 billion yen ($819 million) in the current year, saying repayment from the unit was no longer expected at a time when real estate prices continued to sag.

Matsushita said it will take a special charge of 104 billion yen ($852 million) in parent-company results in the year ending March 31, but said that would be offset by a special gain from stock sales.

For the October-December quarter of 1996, Matsushita's group net profit jumped 35 percent to 45.3 billion yen ($371 million), while operating profit surged 52 percent to 119.7 billion yen ($981 million).
Sales rose 11 percent to 2.03 trillion yen ($16.6 billion).
Communication and industrial equipment sales continued to show strong growth, increasing 28 percent during the quarter, Matsushita said.
"Rapid expansion in mobile communication equipment sales, particularly cellular phones, was a major contributing factor to the growth," the company said in a statement.
Sales of computer peripherals, such as hard-disk drives and personal computer displays, also advanced, it said.
The weak yen also helps Matsushita's overseas sales by reducing foreign currency-denominated sales prices.
Matsushita said it expects record group sales of 7.5 trillion yen ($61.4 billion) for the year ending March 31, up 10 percent from a year earlier.
